source_text: ge-cirran. Take here ge-cerran, ge-cyrran in Dict., and add: A. trans. I. of actual movement. (1) to turn, turn back, change the direction of motion of, (a) a living creature :-- Isaias wæs áwæg farende, ac God hine gecyrde, Hml. S. 18, 422. Se cyningc hý gecyrran wolde eft tó Egyptum, Ors. 1, 7; S. 38, 23. (α) to repulse an advancing enemy (lit. and fig.) :-- Hé ofercuóm &l-bar; gecerde (Iudaeos) conuincit, Mk. p. 4, 19. Men þe þis land bewiston him fyrd ongeán sændon, and hine gecyrdon, Chr. 1091; P. 226, 27. Ðǽr wearð se cyng of France þurh gesmeáh gecyrred, and seó fyrding tóhwearf, 1094; P. 229, 29. (b) a thing :-- Seó strǽl wearð eft gecyrred, and þone mon, þe heó ǽr from sended wæs, sceát. Bl. H. 199, 22. (2) where motion has been caused, to replace, return to a former position :-- Gecerr (-cer, R.) suord in stówe his converte gladium in locum suum, Mt. L. 26, 52. Hæfde Metod égstreám eft gecyrred. Gen. 1415. (3) to go to a person, visit:
